saved_memories.text: Works at a SaaS company that sells wholesale invoicing software to roasters
Is considering raising the Starter plan price from $29 to $39
Company is at $41k MRR with 2.1% churn and 14 new customers this month
Is building a side project: a map of independent coffee roasters
Lives in Austin and is negotiating a lease renewal
Has a colleague named Dana who works on the invoice export service
Has an investor named Sarah who receives monthly updates
Has a customer named Tom, a roaster in Austin, who wants API access
Has a colleague named Marcus who is worried about customer churn from the pricing change
Company's median customer has 50 orders per month

claude_summary.Work context: Works at a B2B SaaS company serving coffee roasters, with invoicing/API features. Colleagues include Dana (engineering) and Marcus (pricing/churn concerns). Reports to an investor named Sarah. Currently deciding whether to raise the Starter plan from $29 to $39, possibly with a usage cap instead. Recently fixed an invoice export bug where line items were dropped for orders with more than 5 items.
claude_summary.Personal context: Lives in Austin, negotiating a lease renewal with a 12% rent increase. Building a side project: a map of independent coffee roasters, currently adding data manually after hitting a rate limit. Decluttering/packing in case of a move.
claude_summary.Top of mind: Recent chats focus on the pricing decision (survey design, churn risk, usage cap), the invoice export bug postmortem and regression tests, preparing for a customer call with Tom, and the investor update for Sarah. Also actively working on the roaster map side project.
claude_summary.Brief history: Over the past two months, the user has been juggling a pricing change investigation, an invoice export bug fix, investor updates, and a side project. They started by debugging the invoice export issue, then moved to pricing strategy, helped a customer (Tom) get started with the API, and prepared an investor update. The invoice bug was reproduced and traced to a likely hardcoded limit/pagination issue. The user also surveyed customers about the price increase and considered a usage cap. Alongside work, they've been building a roaster map, negotiating their lease, and planning to declutter.
